{"id":"3e50b68f-a065-437e-bab5-c28fefaedcfc","object":"chat.completion","created":1786997520,"model":"deepseek-v4-flash","choices":[{"index":0,"message":{"role":"assistant","content":"","reasoning_content":"So the v1 spec set is: deterministic, read_only, retry_safe, idempotent, state_isolated, fault_covered, no_secret_leakage, no_credential_leakage, input_validated, pii_contained, injection_safe. And separately canonical, cost_bounded, etc. from the verifier list.

The issue is that "idempotent" is not discharged. The saga calls co-located handlers and the proof can't establish idempotency. Probably "deterministic" and "retry_safe" would also fail (workflow.call results are nondeterministic). So the right move: drop deterministic, retry_safe, idempotent from the proof set.

Which specs remain that we can discharge?
- state_isolated: no module state → holds.
- fault_covered: saga has compensates for non-last steps... hmm, fault_covered means all fault paths are covered. Saga handles failures via compensation. Maybe it holds. Uncertain.
- result_safe / optional_safe: not in the ZTS502 spec set list, but in the verifiers list; the durable example used "result_safe", "optional_safe", "canonical", "cost_bounded" — these are also v1-ish? ZTS502's help list says "Use one of: deterministic, read_only, retry_safe, idempotent, state_isolated, fault_covered, no_secret_leakage, no_credential_leakage, input_validated, pii_contained, injection_safe." — that's the "help" for unknown names, listing the known v1 spec set. But the durable example used result_safe/optional_safe/canonical/cost_bounded and presumably passed... Actually those may be additional known names. The durable example is a shipped example, so those names must be valid.

OK so which to keep? Let me think about what the saga handler can honestly discharge:
- state_isolated: yes (no module-level state).
- no_secret_leakage, no_credential_leakage: yes.
- input_validated: the key check... borderline; the durable example passes with the same pattern, so keep.
- pii_contained, injection_safe: key doesn't flow to external egress → yes.
- result_safe, optional_safe: no Result/optional misuse → yes.
- canonical: yes if source is canonical.
- cost_bounded: fixed 3-step saga → likely yes.

Uncertain: deterministic (no — call results vary), retry_safe (saga may not be replay-safe from the verifier's view), idempotent (rejected), fault_covered (maybe; saga compensation is exactly fault coverage... but the verifier might not model saga compensation).

Given the veto reported only "idempotent" first, I'll drop deterministic, retry_safe, idempotent and keep the rest. If fault_covered fails, drop it too. Let me iterate.

Actually, let me think about whether to keep "fault_covered". The workflow module summary emphasizes "returns the outcome, including which steps compensated when a later one fails - a handler that discards that result reports success on a saga that rolled back." We don't discard it; we put it in the response body. fault_covered requires all fault paths covered — every workflow.call could fail; the saga handles failure by compensating... The verifier might prove fault_covered because saga handles it. Uncertain. I'll keep it in and let the veto decide — no wait, that risks more churn. Hmm, the veto reports failures one at a time (it seems). Let me keep a reasonably minimal but honest set and iterate if needed.

Let me drop: deterministic, retry_safe, idempotent. Keep: state_isolated, fault_covered, result_safe, optional_safe, no_secret_leakage, no_credential_leakage, input_validated, pii_contained, injection_safe, canonical, cost_bounded.

Hmm wait, but actually, is a Proof even required to be maximally strong? No — claiming fewer specs is fine as long as claimed specs are discharged. So minimal set = what we can discharge. Let me try the set above.","tool_calls":[{"index":0,"id":"call_00_wYQaH7BvC4iiNVi8bM7T9716","type":"function","function":{"name":"propose_change_set","arguments":"{"changes": [{"content": "import { run } from \"zttp:durable\";\nimport { call, saga } from \"zttp:workflow\";\n\nstructural SagaProof<T> = Proof<T,\n  | \"state_isolated\"\n  | \"fault_covered\"\n  | \"result_safe\"\n  | \"optional_safe\"\n  | \"no_secret_leakage\"\n  | \"no_credential_leakage\"\n  | \"input_validated\"\n  | \"pii_contained\"\n  | \"injection_safe\"\n  | \"canonical\"\n  | \"cost_bounded\"\n>;\n\nexport function handler(req: Request): SagaProof<Response> {\n  const key = req.headers.get(\"idempotency-key\");\n  if (key === undefined) {\n    return Response.json({ error: \"missing idempotency-key header\" }, { status: 400 });\n  }\n  return run(key, () => {\n    const outcome = saga([\n      {\n        name: \"reserve\",\n        run: () => call(\"inventory\", { path: \"/reserve\" }),\n        compensate: () => call(\"inventory\", { path: \"/release\" }),\n      },\n      {\n        name: \"charge\",\n        run: () => call(\"billing\", { path: \"/charge\" }),\n        compensate: () => call(\"billing\", { path: \"/refund\" }),\n      },\n      {\n        name: \"ship\",\n        run: () => call(\"shipping\", { path: \"/ship\" }),\n      },\n    ]);\n    return Response.json({ outcome: outcome });\n  });\n}\n", "file": "handler.ts"}]}"}}]},"logprobs":null,"finish_reason":"tool_calls"}],"usage":{"prompt_tokens":28797,"completion_tokens":1399,"total_tokens":30196,"prompt_tokens_details":{"cached_tokens":28288},"completion_tokens_details":{"reasoning_tokens":917},"prompt_cache_hit_tokens":28288,"prompt_cache_miss_tokens":509},"system_fingerprint":"a26a7955944dc5c60445bff77fac9c8e"}
